newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Albania lets West resume satellite transmission.
newsitem.headline: Albania lets West resume satellite transmission.

text.p: Albania on Tuesday informed the European Broadcasting Union (EBU) it could resume satellite transmission of Western television broadcasts out of the troubled Balkan country, an EBU official said.

The Geneva-based EBU restarted transmission after receiving the go-ahead from Albania's PTT. Tony Naets, head of EBU's Eurovision News Services, told Reuters. "We have just been told by Albanian authorities that we can immediately resume satellite operations from Tirana."
Albania pulled the plug on Western television broadcasts out of the country on Monday as a nationwide state of emergency went into effect following a weekend of violence in the south.

The restrictions on EBU, the only organisation providing satellite television feeds to the outside world from Tirana, affected broadcasts by 25 Western companies and channels including Reuters Television, British Broadcasting Corporation, CNN, German networks ARD and ZDF, Italian RAI and French TF1.
"We have in fact started tramsmission again," Naets said.
"To me, they (Albanian authorities) have given in to the pressure regarding the curbs on press freedom," he added.
